title: Move both Dev Teams to the opus alias, and stop two role tabs reading as the same colour

history.detail:
PASS: QA1 gate-1 audit, sprint 44, round 1. Audited commit 3cc6b90 (on fbdaa5f, the sprint start). The sprint file was read fresh at HEAD: it was renamed and amended mid-build (60ed528 added Req 5), and this audit is against the current text. Verdict: PASS.

1. Req 1: both Dev Team agent files now read `model: opus`, the bare alias. The diff across .claude/agents/ contains exactly two model: line changes (sonnet -> opus, one per Dev Team file) and one color: line change. No pinned form anywhere. dev-team-1.md's only change is the model line; dev-team-2.md's second change is Req 5a's own color line, which the mid-build amendment requires.
2. Req 2: CLAUDE.md's table reads opus for both Dev Teams, string-for-string with the frontmatter, with Master Controller/QA1/LiveQA on opus and Pipeman on sonnet.
3. Req 3: the findings doc (docs/sprint-44-dev-team-opus-model-findings.md) meets the "didn't error is not evidence" bar. Version anchor claude 2.1.280; launches go through the real run-role.js headless path rather than a hand-built argv; the verdict comes from the JSON result envelope's own modelUsage/canonicalModel, explicitly not from the model's self-report; two reps on opus both report claude-opus-5-5; and the negative control (temporarily reverting to sonnet) reports claude-sonnet-5, which is what makes the measurement discriminating rather than merely affirmative. Graded CONFIRMED, correctly for a structured, non-model-mediated signal.
4. Req 4: no other agent file's model: line appears in the diff. Pipeman stays sonnet.
5. Req 5:
 - 5a: dev-team-2.md declares cyan and COLOR_MAP gains cyan: 'terminal.ansiCyan'. QA1 keeps yellow; no other role's color moved.
 - 5b: orange stays in the map, with the reason stated (a downstream agent file may declare it; the map is additive, not pruned to current use).
 - 5c: the comment is accurate after the change -- it no longer claims orange is this framework's approximation for Dev Team 2, and now records what the actual defect was (ansiBrightYellow beside QA1's ansiYellow).
 - 5d: QA1 planted, as the criterion requires. Reverting dev-team-2.md to `color: yellow` (a literal duplicate of QA1's) FAILS the new six-distinct test by name. Restored, the suite passes.
6. Req 7: QA1 planted both directions. Editing CLAUDE.md's Dev Team 1 row to sonnet FAILS the new table-vs-frontmatter test, which parses the real table rather than comparing against a hardcoded literal. Changing dev-team-1.md's frontmatter to claude-opus-5-5 also FAILS (one test). So table and frontmatter are genuinely checked against each other, in both directions.
7. Req 6: npm view fully-completely version returns 0.2.18 and package.json is 0.2.19 -- published+1 confirmed at build time -- with a CHANGELOG entry covering Reqs 1-5.
8. Suites at 3cc6b90 in a clean clone: node scripts/launcher_test.js ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED, exit 0. bash scripts/smoke_test.sh ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED, exit 0.
9. The rename leftover Dev Team flagged is exactly what it was described as: the old sprint-44 path is deleted in this commit, git ls-files shows only the current renamed path tracked, and the commit message names the cleanup. Nothing else rode along.

OBSERVATION, not a finding -- but LiveQA should carry it. The Req 5d test asserts six distinct RESOLVED terminal.ansi* values, which is exactly what 5d asks for, and it catches a literal duplicate. It does not catch a near-collision: I planted dev-team-2.md back to `color: orange` and the suite PASSED, because orange resolves to terminal.ansiBrightYellow and QA1's yellow to terminal.ansiYellow -- two distinct values that are the very pair the operator reported as looking alike. This is not a defect in the build: the sprint file's own Risks section already says the test catches declared collisions while only the operator's eyes catch a rendering one, and routes that to LiveQA's live criterion. Recording it so the limit is explicit rather than assumed away, and so nobody later reads a green suite as proof the tabs are visually distinct. If a future sprint wants it mechanical, the shape would be a small set of known-confusable ANSI pairs (yellow/brightYellow being the first), not a broader rule.

FOR LIVEQA. The sprint's own criteria are right, and the screenshot requirement for Req 5 is the correct call given the above. Two additions: report each Dev Team session's model from the structured envelope rather than asking the session what it thinks it is (the findings doc's own method), and include the headless path, since the sprint file asks for it and the headless launcher builds its own arguments.
commit=3cc6b909b4e932226abe93202ba34aecc18719d6 | ci=green: 1 CI run(s) for 3cc6b909b4e932226abe93202ba34aecc18719d6 all completed successfully with real steps executed.

PASS: LiveQA live test, sprint 44, round 1. Verdict: PASS.
Every LiveQA criterion in the sprint file was run against the published 0.2.19, in real scratch installs with real launched sessions, headless and interactive. No defects.

ENVIRONMENT
macOS 26.6.2 arm64, node v24.21.0, npm 11.19.0, git 2.55.0. **Claude Code CLI 2.1.280 at gate time** — it has moved since sprint 43's measurements at 2.1.278, which matters here because this sprint's whole subject is which model a launched session actually runs. 2026-09-22/23. Projects: s44/proj under this session's scratchpad (headless work, driven by LiveQA) and ~/Programming/ws-0219 (VS Code, driven by the operator). Tools: npx, the installed scripts/launcher/run-role.js, git, six real headless launches, one operator-run FC: Start All.

PROVENANCE (registry, not the handoff)
npm dist-tags latest 0.2.19. npm view fully-completely@0.2.19 gitHead 3cc6b909b4e932226abe93202ba34aecc18719d6 == last_shipped_commit. dist.shasum 27fb2e92d8db86a713d580e57b5316941fc7843f == the npm pack download. All 59 published files byte-identical to git show 3cc6b90:<path> (MISMATCHED 0, NOT-IN-COMMIT 0).

REQS 1, 2, 4 — THE DECLARED CONFIGURATION (read from a real install of 0.2.19)
Agent-file frontmatter: master-controller opus/blue, dev-team-1 opus/red, dev-team-2 opus/cyan, qa1 opus/yellow, pipeman sonnet/green, liveqa opus/purple. Both Dev Teams carry the bare alias `opus`, not a pinned version string.
CLAUDE.md's team table: Master Controller opus, Dev Team 1 opus, Dev Team 2 opus, QA1 opus, Pipeman sonnet, LiveQA opus — matching the frontmatter string for string, all six rows.
Pipeman is still sonnet and the other three opus roles are untouched (Req 4).

REQ 3 — WHAT A LAUNCHED SESSION ACTUALLY RUNS ON
Evidence is taken from the structured `modelUsage` key of each headless run's own JSON envelope, not from the model's narration, and from the interactive session header for the operator-run launches.
Headless (installed run-role.js, CLI 2.1.280):
  dev-team-1 -> modelUsage key `claude-opus-5-5`; the session also stated "Opus 5.5, model ID claude-opus-5-5".
  dev-team-2 -> `claude-opus-5-5`; stated "Model: Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5)".
  qa1 (unchanged role, control) -> `claude-opus-5-5`.
  pipeman (unchanged role, control) -> `claude-sonnet-5`; stated "Model: Sonnet 5".
Interactive, real VS Code, FC: Start All in ~/Programming/ws-0219 (operator screenshots):
  Dev Team 1 header: "Claude Code v2.1.280 / Opus 5.5 - Claude Max / @dev-team-1 - ~/Programming/ws-0219".
  Dev Team 2 header: "Opus 5.5 - Claude Max / @dev-team-2".
  Pipeman header: "Sonnet 5 - Claude Max / @pipeman".
So both Dev Teams run on Opus 5.5 on both launch paths, and no role fell back silently. Worth recording for the sprint's own "all five move together" claim: QA1 resolved to claude-opus-5-5 as well, so the bare `opus` alias currently resolves to Opus 5.5 for every role that declares it — the property the sprint predicted, now observed rather than assumed.

REQ 5 — TAB COLOURS
Mechanics (generated .vscode/tasks.json in a fresh install): Master Controller terminal.ansiBlue, Dev Team 1 terminal.ansiRed, Dev Team 2 terminal.ansiCyan, QA1 terminal.ansiYellow, Pipeman terminal.ansiGreen, LiveQA terminal.ansiMagenta. Six roles, six distinct terminal.ansi* values, no collision. `orange: 'terminal.ansiBrightYellow'` is still present in COLOR_MAP (Req 5b), unused by this framework's own roles.
Rendered, which is the evidence the sprint actually asks for since the defect was two declared colours rendering alike: the operator's FC: Start All screenshot shows all seven tabs distinguishable, with Dev Team 2's icon and its `fc:dev-team-2:ws-0219` badge rendering cyan against QA1's yellow. The two no longer read as the same colour.

QA1'S RELAYED NOTES, ADDRESSED
- The Req 5d colour test's blind spot (it catches exact duplicates, not near-miss colours): confirmed as a real limitation, and it is exactly why this round's colour evidence is a rendered screenshot rather than a JSON assertion. Nothing in this release makes the blind spot worse; the near-miss that caused the original complaint (ansiBrightYellow beside ansiYellow) is gone because no role declares orange any more. If a future role is given a colour adjacent to an existing one, the suite will still pass and a human will still have to look. That is a finding for Master Controller's backlog, not a defect in 0.2.19.
- Reporting each Dev Team's model from the structured envelope: done, as above — modelUsage, per role, quoted.

NOT CLAIMED
The sprint's Out of Scope removes the old Req 2a (stating what reads `model:`) and the stale `claude --model opus` example near CLAUDE.md line 75, both moved to a later sprint. I checked neither, deliberately: the build commit predates that amendment and failing a live test over it would cost a publish for documentation the sprint itself defers.

NOTE: sprint 44's file has changed since QA1's PASS (audited hash 9f7401bbb79a..., current 11f6970a1db2...). Recorded, not refused — see this function's own comment for why. If this sprint's own acceptance criteria changed for a real reason, that's worth a fresh /sprint-qa1 look once the live-test loop settles; if it was a cosmetic edit, this note is the whole record of it.
